key_insight: Cluster-weighted loss training helps a 3D CNN focus on difficult regions in solar turbulence data, improving subgrid Reynolds-stress prediction.
engineering_relevance: Better surrogate models for turbulent transport can improve reduced-order modeling of solar convection and other multiscale fluid systems.
method: Train MLP and 3D CNN surrogates on high-resolution StellarBox quiet-Sun simulations.
Use K-Means and hierarchical agglomerative clustering to identify prediction-error clusters.
Reweight the loss by cluster-specific errors to emphasize high-error regions during training.
evidence_signal: Compared with prior baselines, the cluster-weighted CNN achieved 34% lower MSE and a significantly higher R2 score across heights and depths in the solar atmosphere.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the chosen clustering scheme and error distribution, so cluster definitions may need retuning for other datasets or flow regimes.
paper_title: Cluster-Weighted Training of Deep Surrogate Models for Subgrid Turbulent Transport
